chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad Al-Hannat, who said:

We went out, six of us from our companions, to Makkah. So we ignited a great fire in one of the encampments, intending to place upon it pure meat, and we were in Ihram. So a bird passed by us flapping; it was either a dove or like it. So its wings got burnt, and it fell into the fire, so it died. So we were gloomy due to that.

So I went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in Makkah, informed him, and asked him. So he said: 'Upon you is one ransom, the blood of a sheep. You all share in it, because that was from you not by deliberation. And if that had been deliberate from you, in order to catch the prey, so it fell, I would have obligated upon each one of you the blood of a sheep.'
Abu Wallad said, 'And that was from us before we had entered the Haram.'

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.دَمُ شَاةٍ: The blood of a sheep, referring to the slaughter of one sheep as ransom
key_terms.فِدَاء: Ransom or compensation for a religious obligation or prohibition

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in ransom for accidental versus deliberate hunting while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the distinction between accidental and intentional violations of Ihram restrictions, establishing a precedent for collective liability (kaffarah) when a group shares a single cause of transgression. The Imam’s ruling emphasizes that the severity of the ransom scales with the degree of deliberation, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential principle of distinguishing between 'ghayr ta'ammud' (non-deliberate) and 'ta'ammud' (deliberate) acts. This case serves as a foundational example for understanding how shared circumstances mitigate individual burden in ritual law.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abu Wallad Al Hannat who said,

‘We went out, being six of us from our companions, to Makkah. So we ignited a great fire in one of the encampment intending to grill pure meat upon it, and we were in Ihraam. So a bird passed by us flapping. It was either a dove or it’s like. So its wings got burnt, and it fell into the fire, so it died. So we were gloomy due to that.

So I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> in Makkah, and informed him<sup>asws</sup>, and asked him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon you all is one ransom, blood of a sheep. You can all participate in it, because that was from you upon other than deliberation; and had that been deliberate from you in order to catch they prey, so it fell, that would have necessitated upon each one of you, blood of a sheep’.
Abu Wallad said, ‘And that was from us before we had entered the Harram’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from abu Wallad al-Hannat who has said the following: “

In a group one year we went for Makkah and on the way, once we started a large fire to cook a certain amount of meat, while we were in the state of Ihram; and a bird like a pigeon flapping its wings, flew by and hit the fire. Its wings burnt and it died. We became depressed. I then went to see abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, in Makkah, informed him about it and asked about the applicable rule. He (the Imam) said, ‘All of you owe only one sheep as partners because it was without your intentions. Had it been intentional on your part and a prey had fallen in it each one of you would have owed one sheep.’
Abu Wallad has said that it happened before we entered al-Haram (the sacred area).”’
